title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC0RF_1LE0LD_1RC0LB_---1RA_1LB1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC0RF_1LE0LD_1RC0LB_---1RA_1LB1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Sweeps back and forth over a period-10 background (1011011011 and its rightward form 0111101101); a clean zone of it at the left end grows, the rest is a soup of 011, 100, 1 1 0 0 pieces; a halt needs B to read the third of three 0s. Lean proves the sweep rules over the background words and the only local pattern that leads to a halt; no halt in 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 21,745 cells have been visited and 15,171 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.52). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.412).

claims.title: The sweeps cross the background words whole
claims.text: 13 shift rules: for every n and every surrounding tape, a sweep in the stated state crosses n copies of a background word and leaves n copies of its partner, in the stated number of steps (for example L A> (1011011011)^n R ⟶ L (0111101101)^n A> R).

claims.title: The only way to a halt
claims.text: The machine halts only when E reads a 0, and the only way there is B reading a 0 with 0 0 just left of it: three 0s in a row with B on the right one (B and C write 1s and step left, and E meets the last 0.

claims.title: What the tape looks like
claims.text: At the left end there is a clean zone of the period-10 word that grows steadily ((1011011011)173 after 7·106 steps, (1110110110)296 after 2·107); the rest of the tape is a soup of (011)k, (100)k, runs 13, 1 1 0 0 and 0 0 1 0 0.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Pairs of 0s are common in the soup; a third one under B never happened in 10<sup>9</sup> steps, and no invariant forbidding it is known.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LF_1LC0LA_---1RD_1RF1RE_1LF1RD_1LB0RE up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. Sweeps back and forth over a period-10 background (1011011011 and its rightward form 0111101101); a clean zone of it at the left end grows, the rest is a soup of 011, 100, 1 1 0 0 pieces; a halt needs B to read the third of three 0s. This page runs the real machine, explains its sweeps and the words they rewrite, and lists what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 21,745 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
Crossing the background words, proved for every length.
The local pattern every halt must pass through.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.52). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.412).
After 109 steps the tape spans 21,745 cells (10,832 left of the start, 5,217 right), with a density of 1s of 0.698.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Sweeps that rewrite a periodic tape
html: Rightward, A, B and F cross the period-10 word whole (12 steps a copy): A turns 1011011011 into 0111101101; on period 3 A turns 011 into 101 and F turns 101 into 110. Leftward, C and D take them back (about 50 steps a copy), and B, C, D turn 011, 101, 110 into 001, 100, 010.

At the left end there is a clean zone of the period-10 word that grows steadily ((1011011011)173 after 7·106 steps, (1110110110)296 after 2·107); the rest of the tape is a soup of (011)k, (100)k, runs 13, 1 1 0 0 and 0 0 1 0 0.

sections.heading: What one sweep does to the words it crosses
html: A shift rule says that a sweep crosses any number n of copies of a word in one state and leaves n copies of another word behind. These are proved in Lean for every n and every tape around them (lean/Rules.lean); S> is the head in state S on the next cell, L and R the rest of the tape.

sections.heading: The one pattern that halts, and why it has not appeared
html: The machine halts only when E reads a 0, and Lean proves that the only way there is B reading a 0 with 0 0 just left of it: three 0s in a row with B on the right one (B and C write 1s and step left, and E meets the last 0; halt_needs_pattern, lean/Halt.lean). In 109 steps B read a 0 with 1 0 on its left (one 0 short) 38,739 times, all inside the tape.
Pairs of 0s are common in the soup; a third one under B never happened in 109 steps, and no invariant forbidding it is known.
Next step. Find the block structure of the soup (pieces between 00 pairs) and the round-trip map on it.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
